newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Resources steer Australian stocks to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Resources steer Australian stocks to higher close.

text.p: The Australian share market locked away most of its early gains by the close on Friday with a stronger resources group leading the way higher.
The All Ordinaries index climbed 14.5 points to 2,684.2.

Miners managed more than twice the rise of the industrials with the benefits of a weaker Australian dollar and firmer base metals prices boosting the leaders, while the bounce in the bullion price pushed the gold sector to a 1.3 percent gain.
"The golds jumped and you may see the gold price go a little further tonight," said dealer Grant Williams of Sydney brokerage Reynolds and Co.
Others agreed, noting those who had backed the sector after the recent selloff had posted impressive returns.
"The brave ones who backed their judgement when gold was down in the dumps have obviously come out quite well," said broker Dirk van der Struyf of Hartley Poyton.

In the golds, Acacia Resources added 2.9 percent to A$1.38 (US$1.02), sector heavyweight Normandy Mining jumped 2.6 percent to A$1.57, while mooted takeover target Great Central Mines climbed 1.9 percent to A$2.69.

Key miners BHP, up 10 cents to A$18.56, Rio Tinto 24 cents higher at A$21.80, and WMC, 21 cents stronger at A$7.87, all benefited from a weaker Australian dollar and base metals prices that firmed up offshore.

Shares in soft drink maker Coca-Cola Amatil belied the general sluggishness in industrials, rocketing A$1.53 to A$16.58 with traders saying sentiment appeared to have turned for the stock in the absence of major news.

Elsewhere, pay TV operator Australis Media ended up 1.5 cents at 21.5 cents with 6.9 million shares traded after it was reinstated to trading mid-morning. The company said it was still in possible merger talks with rival operator, Foxtel, jointly owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corp and Telstra Corp, the government owned telecommunications carrier.
Expectations for the next week were squarely focussed on second quarter inflation data, due Wednesday, with the hopes for interest rate cuts still alive.

"That will be the issue. The market has been reasonably directionless this week as far as economic news goes, and next week figures come out that we will be focussing closely on," said Daiwa Securities dealer, Michael Sichlau.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about eight to five, while about 28 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
